title: The Role of Systemic Inflammatory Indices in Predicting Cardiovascular Involvement in Children with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
content: Introduction: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked recessive disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration and cardiomyopathy, primarily affecting male children. Besides skeletal muscle involvement, cardiovascular complications significantly increase morbidity and mortality in patients with DMD. Recently, systemic inflammatory indices such as neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) have been proposed as potential markers for cardiovascular risk assessment. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of these inflammatory indices in predicting cardiovascular complications in DMD patients and to examine their relationships with echocardiographic and electrocardiographic findings. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective study, 25 male patients diagnosed with DMD between January 1, 2021, and July 1, 2024, and an age-matched control group of 25 healthy male children were evaluated. Clinical data, including age and treatment protocols, were collected. Hematologic parameters and inflammatory indices (NLR, PLR, MLR, SIRI, SII, and PIV), as well as biochemical data, were analyzed. Cardiovascular assessment was performed using electrocardiography (ECG) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). Statistical analyses included independent t-tests for group comparisons, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis to determine discriminative values, and Pearson correlation analysis to assess relationships between variables. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: The median age of the DMD group was 12 years (range: 5–18), with a mean age of 11.2 ± 4.3 years. The mean age at diagnosis was 4.8 ± 2.6 years. Sixteen percent of patients were wheelchair-dependent, and none required home mechanical ventilation or tracheostomy. Pathological Q waves were the most frequently observed ECG abnormality (24%). Echocardiographic findings showed left ventricular dysfunction or structural anomalies in 16% of the patients. Cardiac treatment including ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, and digoxin was administered to three patients. Hemoglobin levels were significantly higher in the DMD group compared to controls (13.46 ± 1.11 g/dL vs. 12.65 ± 0.84 g/dL; p=0.006), whereas other hematologic parameters did not differ significantly between groups (p>0.05). ROC analysis evaluated the discriminative power of Pro-BNP and PLR for predicting cardiovascular complications and revealed a statistically significant positive correlation between Pro-BNP and PLR (r=0.86, p0.05). Conclusion: This study emphasizes the importance of early detection of cardiovascular complications in patients with DMD. ECG and echocardiographic findings provide valuable information for identifying subclinical cardiac pathology in this population. Nevertheless, the utility of systemic inflammatory indices as cardiovascular risk markers in DMD appears limited. The observed positive correlation between Pro-BNP and PLR draws attention to a possible link between cardiovascular burden and inflammatory response. These findings warrant confirmation through prospective studies involving larger patient cohorts.
